target_customer: Startups and small businesses buying paid advertising on Google, Meta, LinkedIn and TikTok
problem: Startups overpay traditional agencies or lack in-house marketers to run paid campaigns efficiently.
business_model: Agency service fees (one aggregator says from $3,000 monthly) with analytics software; the current site sells a competitor ad intelligence tool at a one-time $250 Pro plan
product_category: AI-assisted performance marketing agency and ad intelligence software

founders.name: Brian Low
founders.background_notes: No background found on the YC page or launch post.

founders.name: Jee
founders.background_notes: Named only as Jee in the YC launch post.

technical_complexity.rationale: Ad campaign operations plus dashboards and a Slack bot built on public ad platform APIs.

defensibility.rationale: Agency services and analytics on public APIs are easy to copy; the YC launch post names traditional agencies, freelancers and in-house teams as the alternative.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copy found in sources.

market_need_then: Startups spend heavily on paid ads; the claim of 10x cheaper agency work and 120+ business customers is the company's own and unverified.

brand_strength.rationale: Name is shared by many unrelated companies (clinics, cannabis, mental health apps) and no brand coverage was found.

pivots.from: Marketing agency for startups with analytics dashboard (also began as a SaaS product per the launch post)
pivots.to: Competitor ad intelligence platform (current usekaya.com site)
pivots.why: Not stated; inferred from the current site and the launch post, date unknown

outcome_analysis: Kaya launched as an AI-assisted marketing agency for startups in 2021 and claimed 120+ clients, but no funding, revenue or exit was found. The current site sells an ad intelligence tool, which suggests a shift in offering, so the outcome is an active small company with insufficient public data to judge.
notes: YC lists Kuala Lumpur and some listings say London; location conflicts. CB Insights lists $500K on 1/1/2021, a likely placeholder, not recorded. Competitors named in the launch post are generic categories only (traditional agencies, freelancers, in-house), and dated named rivals were not found, so the list is empty. Pricing sources conflict ($3,000 monthly versus $59 per month tool). No shutdown or acquisition news found. The Kaya blog on kaya-toast.web.app appears self-published and was not relied on. Completeness pass: a convertible note of 500K dated 2021-01-01 is recorded from CB Insights alone; it rests on a single database and the Jan 1 date looks like a placeholder. Extruct lists a 2.6M seed in 2022 and Seedtable a 500K pre-seed, both unconfirmed and possibly other entities, so not recorded.
